title: Hierarchical batch hedger and attention probe for continuous batching
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: reduce end-to-end p95/p99 tail latency for multi-tenant continuous streaming workloads by introducing a hierarchical admission controller (per-tenant + global) that supports hedged micro-slices, and by adding a lightweight attention probe that guides runtime kernel selection before large prefill batches are admitted.

Context: recent spikes from long-sequence conversational sessions cause large prefill batches to form that lock expensive attention kernels and create long decode tails for other tenants. We suspect two contributors: (1) suboptimal kernel selection for mixed sequence lengths, and (2) admission policy that only considers queue depth and not downstream kernel fit or attention warmup state.

Approach:
- Hierarchical admission controller: per-tenant credit buckets + global soft-throttles. New admission step will compute an expected kernel-fit vector based on the request sequence-length distribution and a quick attention-probe score (see below). If the expected kernel mix would push latency beyond SLO, the request will be hedged into a micro-slice or delayed up to X ms depending on priority.
- Hedged micro-slices: instead of admitting a full prefill to the decode stage, we allow a small speculative decode (N tokens) on a faster kernel/quantized path. If the speculative work meets quality thresholds, it proceeds; otherwise, the full kernel path is used and the speculative work is merged. This reduces tail amplification from large blocking kernels.
- Attention probe: a cheap attention-profile pass (sublinear in sequence length) that yields a small vector of "attention hotness" signals (sparsity, average head norm estimates) used to predict whether a given request will trigger heavy attention kernels or be satisfied by lighter kernels. Probe runtime cost targeted < 1ms at 2k seq.
- Kernel-swapper policy: runtime will use the probe output + recent kernel latency histograms to select a preferred kernel variant (fast-quantized vs conservative-accurate) and, when necessary, pre-warm KV cache paths or schedule prefetching to reduce first-token latency.

Success metrics: p95 and p99 across mixed workloads, measured on canary cluster with representative tenant mix. Target: reduce p95 by >=25% and p99 by >=20% for the impacted tail class without increasing average token cost by more than 3%.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Probe accuracy vs cost: overly conservative probes will cause more hedging/delays; overly permissive probes will misroute to slow kernels. We will tune thresholds with real traffic.
- Quality regression risk from speculative decoding on quantized kernels. We will gate speculative acceptance with per-prompt quality heuristics and scoreboard sampling.
- Complexity in admission accounting: hierarchical credits add bookkeeping; we will reuse existing tenant quota primitives where possible.

Related artifacts: design doc and initial microbench results linked in attachments.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout shows p95 reduction >=25% on mixed long/short workload compared to baseline within 2 weeks
No customer-visible correctness regressions in sampled generation audits (manual + automated checks)
Kernel-swapper picks non-default kernel for >=15% of prefill cases where probe predicts heavy attention and reduces first-decode latency
Hedged micro-slice flow integrates with existing KV cache merge protocol and has documented merge semantics
End-to-end cost per token increase <=3% on average for canary traffic
comments: 2026-02-11 - AC: Kickoff meeting. Agreed scope: implement probe + admission glue first, then hedged micro-slices. Luis to prototype probe and a simulator to estimate misclassification cost.

2026-02-18 - LM: Prototype probe implemented (runtime/attn_probe). Quick simulation shows probe precision ~0.78 at recall 0.85 for heavy-attention detection on synthetic dataset. Simulator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7421
2026-02-25 - PM Priya Kapoor: Please ensure SLO config knobs are exposed in Console for per-tenant overrides and that rollout can be toggled per cluster.

2026-03-02 - LM: Initial hierarchical admission shim checked into canary branch. It reuses tenant credits from quota service; added soft-throttle heuristics and micro-slice queue. Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7499

2026-03-05 - Design review (Luis/Ava/Marco): Decided to keep probe as best-effort observable signal; admission must treat probe as advisory (not a hard gate). Marco requested telemetry for probe confidence and kernel-change rate.

2026-03-09 - QA: Ran integration test harness with 50/50 long/short mix. Baseline p95=420ms, after probe+admission p95=310ms, p99 improved from 980ms to 760ms in initial runs. Investigating two regression cases where quantized speculative decode produced repeated hallucination patterns — gating added.
2026-03-12 - LM: Added merge protocol to reconcile speculative outputs with full decode. Edge-case: user-supplied stop tokens need deterministic handling; spec updated in design doc.

2026-03-14 - AC: Preparing canary rollout plan. Need approvals from SRE for autoscaling thresholds and from Security for potential side-channel risks of the attention probe. Open blocker: security review on probe fingerprinting risk (assigned to Sarah Gomez).
